title: Securities Trading Policy (Exhibit 19.1 to the Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 30 June 2026)

tiers.name: Covered Persons
tiers.description: All members of the Board of Directors, directors emeriti, employees, and those consultants and independent advisors designated and notified by the Company, until they are no longer affiliated with the Company and no longer aware of material, non-public information; expressly includes their family members and controlled entities. This tier carries the substantive bans (no trading on MNPI, no short sales, no derivatives, no hedging or pledging, no margin purchases).

tiers.name: Section 16 Reporting Persons
tiers.description: Members of the Board of Directors, directors emeriti and certain executive officers who are subject to the reporting and short-swing profit provisions of Section 16 of the Exchange Act. Informed of their status by the General Counsel or designee. Subject additionally to black-out periods, the six-month holding period and pre-clearance.

tiers.name: Designated Individuals
tiers.description: Other Covered Persons designated by the Company from time to time and notified of that status; subject to the same additional prohibitions and procedures as Section 16 Reporting Persons. The Company may in its discretion also subject other Covered Persons who gain access to material, non-public information to these prohibitions for such period as it deems appropriate.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Defined collective term for Section 16 Reporting Persons, Designated Individuals and their family members and controlled entities. This is the tier to which quarterly and special black-out periods, the six-month minimum holding period and General Counsel pre-clearance apply.

tiers.name: family members and controlled entities
tiers.description: Family members who reside with the Covered Person (spouse, domestic partner, child, child away at college, stepchildren, grandchildren, parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings and in-laws), anyone else living in the household other than household employees, and family members outside the household whose transactions in Company securities are directed by or subject to the influence or control of the Covered Person; plus entities such as trusts and corporations that the Covered Person or their family members manage or over which they have or share control over investment decisions. The Covered Person is responsible for their compliance.

windows.start_anchor: close of the market on the fourteenth (14th) day prior to the close of any fiscal quarter
windows.end_anchor: after one full Trading Day following the release of the Company's quarterly or annual financial results for that quarter

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may implement additional black-out periods from time to time with regard to certain Covered Persons or groups who are aware of non-public information regarding potentially significant matters. They are confidential: any person made aware of such an additional black-out must not disclose its existence to anyone inside or outside the Company. The Board of Directors or the General Counsel may modify the Policy or grant an exception where circumstances make it appropriate.

rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: Flat ban on investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles. No venue limitation, so OTC puts and calls written or bought with a bank are caught as squarely as listed ones, and the ban applies to every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities regardless of whether the underlying shares are vested. The only carve-out is holding and exercising options, RSUs or other derivative securities granted under the Company's own equity compensation plans.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall invest in Company-based derivative securities. “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.detail: The single express permission: holding and exercising Company-granted options, RSUs and other plan derivative securities is not prohibited, and the grant, award, vesting and settlement of those instruments is not a 'transaction' at all. This is a carve-out for the Company's own instruments only and does not extend to third-party derivatives over the resulting shares.
rules.evidence: However, holding and exercising stock options, restricted stock units or other derivative securities granted under the Company’s equity compensation plans is not prohibited by this Policy.

rules.detail: One-sentence absolute ban on hedging any equity compensation or Company securities held directly. No definition of 'hedging' is given, no clearance or exception route is offered within the clause, and no distinction is drawn between unvested, vested-locked and vested-unrestricted holdings. A collar is the paradigm hedge and is prohibited on this clause alone, independently of the derivatives ban.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging); Appendix A cl.4
rules.detail: Vesting does not release the hedging ban: it reaches 'Company securities that they hold directly', not merely unvested equity compensation. Appendix A reinforces the position for anyone using a Rule 10b5-1 plan, requiring that no corresponding or hedging transaction has been entered into or altered over the plan securities and that none be entered into while the plan is in effect.
rules.evidence: No Hedging. Covered Persons may not have entered into or altered a corresponding or hedging transaction or position with respect to the securities subject to the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan and must agree not to enter into any such transaction while the Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan is in effect.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Investments in Derivatives)
rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards, variable prepaid forwards and zero-cost collars are not named. Each is caught twice over: as a hedge of Company securities held directly, and as an investment in a Company-based derivative security. A monetisation that instead borrows against the shares is caught by the pledging limb. There is no clearance path that cures a prohibited transaction; only the Board or General Counsel exception power in section 2.B could.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.detail: Outright ban, with a definition wide enough to catch a sale of owned shares that is not settled by delivery within twenty days ('short against the box'). Relevant to any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg of a collar structure.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall engage in the short sale of the Company’s securities. A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a “short against the box”).

rules.detail: Securities lending and rehypothecation are nowhere named, and the Policy has no general 'dealing' definition that sweeps them in. In practice a lend that enabled non-delivery against a sale would engage the twenty-day short-against-the-box limb, and for a Restricted Person any transaction, direct or indirect, in Company securities requires pre-clearance.

rules.section: 2.A (No Investments in Derivatives of the Company's Securities)
rules.detail: CFDs, swaps and total return swaps are not named, but the derivative-securities definition is open-ended ('or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security') and the prohibition is expressed as non-exhaustive, so a cash-settled contract for difference over News Corp stock or CDIs falls within it. A short CFD would also engage the short sale ban.
rules.evidence: “Derivative Securities” are options, warrants, stock appreciation rights or similar rights whose value is derived from the value of an equity security, such as the Company’s common stock. This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.

rules.section: 2.A (No Margin Purchases; No Hedging or Pledging)
rules.detail: Two overlapping bans. Borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase Company securities is prohibited outright, with a narrow carve-out for cashless option exercises under the Company's equity plans. Borrowing against Company securities already held is prohibited under the pledging limb. Neither has a clearance or hardship route.
rules.evidence: No Covered Person shall purchase the Company’s securities on margin. This means such persons are prohibited from borrowing from a brokerage firm, bank or other entity in order to purchase the Company’s securities (other than in connection with “cashless” exercises of stock options under the Company’s equity compensation plans).

rules.detail: Pledging any equity compensation or directly held Company securities is banned in the same sentence as hedging. The ban is on the act of pledging, not on the underlying loan, so it bites on the security interest a lender would take over the collared shares. It is expressed by reference to securities 'that they hold directly', which leaves indirectly held securities textually unaddressed even though family members and controlled entities are themselves Covered Persons.
rules.evidence: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.A (No Hedging or Pledging; No Margin Purchases)
rules.detail: The Policy never uses the phrase 'secured financing', but any loan secured on News Corp shares or CDIs requires a pledge, and pledging is prohibited for all Covered Persons and their family members and controlled entities without regard to vesting, tier or amount. There is no margin-loan-only qualifier, no threshold, no notification alternative and no disclosure regime; the only relief is the general Board or General Counsel exception power.
rules.evidence: Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.

rules.section: 2.B (No Trading in the Company's Securities on a Short-Term Basis)
rules.detail: Hard six-month minimum holding period for any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person, reinforced by the Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement rule. Same-day cashless option exercises are excluded provided there were no open-market purchases in the preceding six months. Any collar whose put leg could be exercised, or whose shares could be delivered, within six months of an open-market purchase would breach this.
rules.evidence: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.

rules.detail: The six-month holding period sits in section 2.B, which applies only to Restricted Persons. Covered Persons who are neither Section 16 Reporting Persons nor Designated Individuals have no holding period or speculative-trading restriction beyond the MNPI, short sale, derivatives, hedging, pledging and margin bans.

Restricted Persons inherit the outright derivatives ban and, even for permitted transactions, are additionally barred during quarterly and special black-out periods and must pre-clear with the General Counsel. Derivative securities including put and call options are expressly within the definition of the Company's securities to which section 2 applies, so nothing in the pre-clearance machinery converts a prohibited derivative into a permitted one.
rules.evidence: the following policies apply to all transactions (including gifts), direct or indirect, in all of the Company’s securities, including, but not limited to, the Company’s Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities).

rules.detail: Family members and controlled entities (trusts and corporations managed by, or over whose investment decisions control is held or shared by, the Covered Person or their family members) are themselves Covered Persons, so the hedging, pledging, derivatives, short sale and margin bans apply to them directly. Routing a collar or a secured loan through a family trust or holding company therefore does not escape the prohibitions, and the Covered Person is made responsible for their compliance.
rules.evidence: This Policy applies to ... (i) such persons’ “family members” and (ii) entities (such as trusts and corporations) which such foregoing persons or their family members manage or over which they or their family members have or share control over investment decisions (“controlled entities”). You are responsible for ensuring that your family members and controlled entities comply with this policy.

clearance.approver: the Company's General Counsel or his or her designee (for the General Counsel's own Rule 10b5-1 plan, the Chief Financial Officer)
clearance.evidence: the proposed transaction or stock option exercise must be pre-cleared with either the Company’s General Counsel or his or her designee, even if the proposed transaction or stock option exercise is to take place outside of the Black-Out Period. If the transaction or stock option exercise is cleared to proceed, the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.
If a Restricted Person is contemplating a transaction or stock option exercise in the Company’s securities, the proposed transaction or stock option exercise must be pre-cleared

carve_outs: Same day “cashless” exercises of stock options, provided that there were no previous purchase transactions on the open market within six (6) months of the exercise date
short_term.evidence: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months. Note that the SEC’s short swing profit rules already penalize Section 16 Reporting Persons who sell any Company securities within six (6) months of a purchase.

exceptions.evidence: the exercise of Company stock options if no shares are to be sold or if there is a “net exercise” (i.e., the use of the underlying shares to pay the exercise price and/or tax withholding obligations), except the exercise is still subject to pre-clearance procedures, if applicable

the grant, award, vesting and/or settlement of Company stock options, restricted stock or restricted stock units; the withholding of shares to satisfy a tax withholding obligation upon the vesting/settlement of restricted stock or restricted stock units

transferring shares to an entity that does not involve a change in the beneficial ownership of the shares (for example, transferring shares from one brokerage account to another brokerage account that a Covered Person controls)
sales of the Company’s securities as a selling stockholder in a registered public offering in accordance with applicable securities laws
any other purchase of Company securities from the Company or sales of Company securities to the Company in accordance with applicable securities and state laws
purchases of Company stock in its 401(k) plan resulting from periodic contributions of money pursuant to a payroll deduction election.

transactions in mutual funds that are invested in Company securities as long as (i) the Covered Person does not control the investment decisions on individual stocks within the fund or portfolio and (ii) Company securities do not represent a substantial portion of the assets of the fund or portfolio.

exceptions.approver: General Counsel (or the Chief Financial Officer for the General Counsel's own plan), in writing, at least five Trading Days before entry
exceptions.evidence: a transaction may be exempt from this prohibition if it is made pursuant to a written trading plan that has been approved in writing in line with this Policy and entered into in advance of a Black-Out Period ... For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.

exceptions.approver: the Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel
exceptions.evidence: This Policy may be modified or an exception granted with approval of the Company’s Board of Directors or the Company’s General Counsel, where the circumstances make such modification or exception appropriate, in compliance with applicable law.

external_documents: Proxy Statement, 'Compensation Discussion and Analysis—Securities Trading Policy and Prohibition on Hedging of News Corporation Stock' (incorporated by reference into Item 10 of the Form 10-K as the Company's insider trading policy disclosure)
The Company's equity compensation plans (govern grant, vesting, net and cashless exercise)
The Company's 401(k) retirement savings plan, pension plan and other similar plans
The Company's standardized form of Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plan, which the Company may require Covered Persons to use
SEC Rule 10b5-1, Section 16 of the Exchange Act and Rule 144 of the Securities Act
exemption_authority: The Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel may modify the Policy or grant an exception where the circumstances make it appropriate and it is in compliance with applicable law (section 2.B). This is the only relief valve; there is no hardship, financial-need or court-order exception, and the clause is stated in the context of black-out periods but is drafted at Policy level. The General Counsel and the Legal Department also administer pre-clearance and the Rule 10b5-1 guidelines.
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities law: Exchange Act section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5, Section 16 reporting and short-swing profit liability, Rule 10b5-1 affirmative defence and its 2022 cooling-off, certification, overlapping-plan and single-transaction conditions, and Securities Act Rule 144
Nasdaq Global Select Market (primary listing venue; 'Trading Day' means a day on which the Nasdaq Stock Market is open for trading)

ASX: the Policy expressly treats CHESS Depositary Interests representing Class A and Class B Common Stock as Company securities, but states no separate Australian law, ASX Listing Rule 12.9 or Corporations Act overlay

bespoke_clauses.clause: No Hedging or Pledging. Covered Persons are prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single sentence kills both legs of a funded collar at once: the put and call are a hedge and the loan security is a pledge, for every Covered Person and their family members and controlled entities, with no vesting, tier or size qualifier and no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities that they hold directly
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only textual soft spot in the ban is the words 'hold directly', but the Scope section makes family members and controlled entities Covered Persons in their own right, so an indirect holding structure does not create a workable exemption and any attempt would need General Counsel confirmation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition includes, but is not limited to, trading in Company-based put or call option contracts, trading in straddles and the like.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC bilateral put and call with a bank is caught exactly as a listed option would be, and a two-leg collar is closer to a 'straddle and the like' than a plain option, so there is no exchange/OTC arbitrage.

bespoke_clauses.clause: all of the Company's securities, including ... CHESS Depositary Interests representing the Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock and derivative securities (including stock options, put or call options and other similar securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar written over ASX-quoted CDIs rather than Nasdaq-listed common stock is inside the Policy, so the ASX line offers no separate route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, transactions pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans that are effected in accordance with this Policy may occur notwithstanding the other prohibitions included herein.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the widest permission in the document and could in principle cover disposals inside a black-out, but Appendix A clause 4 expressly forbids any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities, so a 10b5-1 plan is an alternative to a collar, not a wrapper for one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy may be modified or an exception granted with approval of the Company's Board of Directors or the Company's General Counsel, where the circumstances make such modification or exception appropriate, in compliance with applicable law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only conceivable path to a funded collar is a bespoke Board or General Counsel exception, which would sit against a proxy-disclosed anti-hedging commitment and would still have to survive Section 16, Rule 144 and short-swing profit analysis.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A short sale is a sale of securities not owned by the seller or, if owned, not delivered against such sale within twenty (20) days thereafter (a 'short against the box').
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any physically settled forward or delayed-delivery leg where shares are not delivered within twenty days is a prohibited short sale, which forecloses prepaid variable forward structures as well as collars.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Additional black-out periods may be implemented from time to time ... Any person made aware of any such additional black-out period shall not disclose the existence of the black-out to anyone else inside or outside the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed event-driven black-outs can freeze entry, roll, unwind or settlement at any time and cannot be flagged to a counterparty bank, so any structure would need documentation permitting silent suspension.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the transaction must be executed within five Trading Days after the approval is obtained, but regardless may not be executed if the Restricted Person acquires material, non-public information concerning the Company or its securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even for permitted transactions the pricing window is five Trading Days and clearance falls away automatically on receipt of inside information, so a bank must accept a short, revocable execution window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Company securities purchased on the open market by a Restricted Person must be held for a minimum of six (6) months.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Combined with Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement, this rules out any collar tenor or early unwind that could put a disposal within six months of an open-market purchase by a director or Section 16 officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The prohibition against trading during the Black-Out Period also prohibits the fulfillment of 'limit orders' by any broker for Restricted Persons, and the brokers with whom any such 'limit order' is placed must be informed of such prohibition at the time such 'limit order' is placed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Automatic third-party execution is treated as the executive's own trading, so a lender's or counterparty's price-triggered sale or delivery during a black-out would be a Policy breach attributed to the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: transferring shares to an entity that does not involve a change in the beneficial ownership of the shares (for example, transferring shares from one brokerage account to another brokerage account that a Covered Person controls)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving shares into a collateral or custody account is not itself a 'transaction' needing clearance, but the security interest granted over them is still a prohibited pledge, so the transfer carve-out gives no help.

bespoke_clauses.clause: After termination of employment or other service, any Covered Person who is aware of material, non-public information regarding the Company or its securities is prohibited from trading in Company securities until that information has become public or is no longer material.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A departing executive cannot assume that leaving releases the restrictions in time to unwind or settle a structure.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a News Corp director or executive under this Policy. Both legs fail independently: section 2.A bans investing in Company-based derivative securities, expressly including put and call option contracts and straddles, with no venue limit so OTC options with a bank are caught, and the same section prohibits Covered Persons from hedging or pledging any equity compensation or Company securities they hold directly, which defeats the loan security as well as the hedge. The bans apply to every Covered Person and, through the Scope section, to family members and controlled entities, so a trust or holding company does not help, and the only carve-out is holding and exercising Company-granted options and RSUs. Layered on top for Section 16 Reporting Persons and Designated Individuals are quarterly black-outs running from fourteen days before quarter end until one Trading Day after results, General Counsel pre-clearance valid for five Trading Days, and a six-month minimum holding period on open-market purchases reinforced by short-swing profit disgorgement. The only conceivable route is a bespoke modification or exception approved by the Board of Directors or the General Counsel under section 2.B; absent that, the realistic alternative is a pre-cleared Rule 10b5-1 sale plan, which may trade notwithstanding the other prohibitions but whose Appendix A conditions expressly forbid any corresponding or hedging position over the plan securities.
